chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from an-Nadr ibn Suwayd and Ahmad ibn Muhammad from 'Asim ibn Humayd from Muhammad ibn Qays from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

I heard him say: 'Any woman who is divorced, then her husband dies before her waiting period ('iddah) expires, and she has not become permanently forbidden to him, then she inherits him. Then she observes the waiting period of the one whose husband died for her. And if she dies while in her waiting period and has not become permanently forbidden to him, then he inherits her. And if he is killed, she inherits from his blood-money (diyah), and if she is killed, he inherits from her blood-money, provided that one of them did not kill the other.'

key_terms.اَلْمُتَوَفَّى عَنْهَا: The one whose [husband] died for her
key_terms.عِدَّةُ: Waiting period ('Iddah) after divorce or death
key_terms.لَمْ تَحْرُمْ عَلَيْهِ: Has not become permanently forbidden to him

ai.seo_question: What are the inheritance and 'iddah rules for a divorced woman if her husband dies before her waiting period ends?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Baqir clarifies the legal status of a woman in the intermediate stage of divorce (khula' or talaq before final revocation), establishing that she retains full inheritance rights and observes the widow's four-month ten-day waiting period. It further extends these reciprocal rights to blood-money (diyah), ensuring equitable compensation unless one party murdered the other, a nuance critical in Shia jurisprudence for determining the completeness of the marital bond during this transitional phase.
